before.nesnd_small_states.2.far_south: Australia's population and processing centres now maintain effective links with local production in New Zealand. Working ports carry goods to market. These industries support the Far South's growth and provide revenue for local services.
before.nesnd_small_states.2.burma: Production in the upper country around $STATE_MANDALAY$ and the lower country at $STATE_PEGU$ now reaches the market through existing transport. Better earnings for farmers and merchants support livelihoods and give the government more room to provide administration and education.
before.nesnd_small_states.2.siam: Production outside Bangkok is now linked to the population and fiscal centre. The existing army still draws on national revenue, while local development raises the question of how administration and education should be distributed.
before.nesnd_small_states.6.far_south: Production and shipping now link Australia and New Zealand, while schools and public offices can sustain local services. The government has more revenue and trained personnel with which to conduct foreign affairs and plan development in both regions.
before.nesnd_small_states.6.burma: Production and public services have gained a stable footing in the upper country and the lower reaches around $STATE_PEGU$. Markets and transport linking the two have increased public revenue, while schools train new personnel. Burma can use these strengths to seek better terms abroad.
before.nesnd_small_states.6.siam: Production, public services and defence now connect Bangkok with the provinces. Government revenue must support the army as well as schools and local administration. Its allocation remains a matter of national debate.
before.nesnd_small_livelihood_journal_reason: Farmers, artisans and merchants bear the costs of rent, taxation and changing markets. Greater autonomy requires income from local production and people trained to staff schools and public offices. Foreign investment can bring money and expertise, and support from an overlord can ease the burden, but the country must still sustain itself through local work and enterprise.

before.nesnd_small_economy_journal_reason: Existing industries can sustain the country if they provide work, earn a profit and reach their markets.
before.nesnd_small_governance_journal_reason: The provinces need teachers, administrators and reliable public funding. Schools and government services must extend beyond the capital if more people are to gain an education and enter new occupations.
before.nesnd_small_regional_economy_journal_rea: The population center and the surrounding regions have different strengths in agriculture, mining, fishing, forestry and manufacturing. Transport links to the market can turn these resources into industries that supply and support one another.
before.nesnd_small_regional_governance_journal_: Public revenue must support more than the capital. Both regions need functioning administration, while schools and universities prepare residents for new occupations.
before.nesnd_small_order_journal_reason: Independence or extensive autonomy gives the government more authority, along with responsibility for trade, law and defence. Local producers need dependable customers, schools need funding, and the borders need reliable allies and troops.

before.nesnd_small_paused_status: Some conditions are unmet this month. Previously earned qualifying months are retained.
before.nesnd_small_dispute_journal_reason: Hardship and restrictive laws have given a local movement support. The government may permit organisation, promise legal reform or use the police to suppress it. Each choice affects particular interests.
before.nesnd_small_dispute_status: The movement is seeking support. A promise of reform is fulfilled only by an actual change in law.
before.nesnd_small_public_desc: Administration and industry need people able to take on new duties. A year of public spending can help build those skills.
before.nesnd_small_public_tt: Pay the weekly quote fixed when the programme begins for 12 months. Qualifications and tax capacity receive temporary help. The programme cannot be cancelled early or duplicated.
before.nesnd_small_specialise_button_desc: Merchants and guilds seek wider outlets within the present market, with greater room to manage local business.
before.nesnd_small_specialise_button_tt: For 12 months, qualifications improve and authority falls by 25. The arrangement ends if the market owner changes or the country controls its own market.

before.nesnd_small_own_market_button_desc: Market autonomy requires more than permission: producers still need inputs, transport and customers.
before.nesnd_small_own_market_button_tt: Choose a 12-month policy without immediately changing market ownership. Public investment becomes available after actual market autonomy. Qualifying industries must have no input shortages.

before.nesnd_small_states.2.d: Production has provided a steadier livelihood for farmers and workers. These activities support revenue and skills, giving local development firmer foundations.
before.nesnd_small_states.3.d: Administration and education can now shoulder more local responsibilities. New occupations and knowledge give the government a practical basis for greater autonomy; how it uses them remains a political choice.
before.nesnd_small_states.4.d: The former owner no longer directs the country's market. The temporary arrangement with merchants and guilds has ended. Existing industries remain, while supply and transport must adapt to the new market relationship.
before.nesnd_small_states.5.d: Years have passed without laws, markets and defence jointly sustaining the intended arrangement. The government may try again when conditions improve. Existing industries, schools and laws remain.
before.nesnd_small_states.6.d: Local production, schools and administration have gained a stable footing, while foreign agreements have given the country greater room to act. The government has more revenue and trained personnel with which to face changing markets, provincial disputes and pressure from abroad.
before.nesnd_small_states.11.d: The promised reform has become law. Its beneficiaries have reason to believe that their demands can be answered, while established interests face a new distribution of benefits.
before.nesnd_small_states.12.d: The promised term has passed, and the old law still binds those who sought change. The government's failure to act has deepened local resentment.
before.nesnd_small_states.10.land: Rents and debt bondage weigh on local farmers and labourers. Land reformers are organising them to change who controls land and work. The government must decide how to respond to this existing movement.
before.nesnd_small_states.10.labor: Hardship among labourers has strengthened the labour movement. Wages, hours and protection at work have become matters of dispute. The government's approach to organisation and law will affect the balance between workers and employers.
before.nesnd_small_states.10.representation: An existing liberal or radical movement is seeking local support. Caste or political restrictions prevent residents from participating in public affairs. Demands for change place the distribution of power under pressure.

before.nesnd_small_states.20.autonomy: The government of [SCOPE.sCountry('canon_sender').GetName] argues that its economy and administration can bear greater responsibilities and asks us to relax our control over its internal affairs. Acceptance will increase its autonomy.
before.nesnd_small_states.20.independence: [SCOPE.sCountry('canon_sender').GetName] asks to end direct subjection peacefully and assume responsibility for its own affairs. Relinquishing overlordship will change both countries' rights and obligations and may settle the dispute through negotiation.
before.nesnd_small_states.20.market: [SCOPE.sCountry('canon_sender').GetName] asks to control its own market. Local merchants and producers would take responsibility for supplies and customers. We must decide whether to grant that right.
before.nesnd_small_states.20.defence: [SCOPE.sCountry('canon_sender').GetName] proposes a defensive treaty. Both countries will assume the obligations of its effective terms, and war may put their economic and diplomatic ties to the test.

before.nesnd_small_refuse_tt: Refuse the proposal. Rejecting a request for greater autonomy increases the subject's Liberty Desire and harms relations.

after.nesnd_small_states.2.far_south: The sea between Australia and New Zealand has become a common trading route for their producers. Ports can hire workers and local industries have found outlets for their goods, giving the Far South more than a single centre of production on which to depend.\n\nFarmers and labourers have firmer livelihoods, and the government can draw revenue from their work. The schools and local services it hopes to maintain will depend on the goods crossing these waters, and on the people who produce them.
after.nesnd_small_states.2.burma: Viable industries have taken root in the upper country around $STATE_MANDALAY$ and the lower reaches at $STATE_PEGU$. Transport carries their produce to market, providing farmers, labourers and merchants with a steadier living.\n\nThese links between the upper and lower country give the government the means to attend to local affairs. With revenue to support them, administration and education can become more than aspirations. The division of that revenue will help determine how much each region gains from this growth.
after.nesnd_small_states.2.siam: More dependable market links now connect production in Bangkok and the provinces. The centres of population and wealth need goods from elsewhere, while provincial producers need customers if they are to pay wages and taxes.\n\nThese ties bring the government more revenue, along with competing demands on its use. The army needs supplies, and the provinces need schools and public services. Those whose work fills the treasury will expect the state to take an interest in their lives.
after.nesnd_small_states.6.far_south: Production and shipping between Australia and New Zealand can now support public affairs in both regions. Offices have staff and education has a firmer footing. The Far South is acquiring the revenue and trained people it needs to sustain its own affairs.\n\nThe government can speak with greater confidence abroad. Whoever sits across the negotiating table, the wealth created by these communities and the public institutions they maintain give substance to our claim to greater independence.
after.nesnd_small_states.6.burma: Production, transport and public services have gained a more secure footing in the upper country and the lower reaches around $STATE_PEGU$. The government has revenue, and local people can undertake administration and teaching. Relations between the two regions now extend well beyond the exchange of goods.\n\nBurma can draw on these resources to conduct its own affairs. Foreign relations will still require care, but the country has more wealth and trained people on which to rely when faced with demands from abroad.
after.nesnd_small_states.6.siam: Production in Bangkok and the provinces can now sustain public services, with firmer foundations for administration, education and defence. Government revenue is becoming the means to uphold our autonomy.\n\nThis achievement will hardly end disagreement. The provinces want schools and improvements, the army requires dependable supplies, and the central government has expenses of its own. The argument now concerns what kind of country this revenue should sustain as much as where the money is to come from.
after.nesnd_small_livelihood_journal_reason: A small country's freedom of action often rests on the livelihoods of ordinary people. Farmers must be able to pay their taxes, labourers to find work, and merchants to carry goods to willing buyers before the government can afford administration, education and defence. When producers are overwhelmed by rent, debt and unemployment, every grand undertaking makes another demand on people who can scarcely bear it.\n\nForeign capital can bring money and knowledge, and an overlord's support may ease some burdens. To have a stronger voice in these relationships, the country needs viable local industries and opportunities for its people to learn new skills. The means to conduct affairs of state begin in these seemingly modest concerns.

after.nesnd_small_economy_journal_reason: Government expenditure rests on the work of people who must first earn their own living. Farmers need buyers for their harvests, artisans and labourers need employment, and goods need roads and ports to reach their customers. A lasting obstruction at any point spreads hardship to others.\n\nOur existing industries provide a place to begin. When these businesses can employ people and earn an income, households will have something to put aside, and the country will have the means to consider a more distant future.
after.nesnd_small_governance_journal_reason: As industries begin to earn an income, the provinces need more people capable of managing public affairs. Tax collection, local services and the education of children cannot depend indefinitely on favours among a handful of acquaintances. Teachers and administrators need dependable salaries, while those pursuing an education need some prospect of employment when it is complete.\n\nEstablishing these institutions will give the government a lasting claim on local support. At least some of the taxes people surrender should return to them as public services on which they can depend.
after.nesnd_small_regional_economy_journal_rea: Centres of population and wealth need the produce of other regions, whose farms, mines, fisheries, forests and workshops in turn need wider markets. However plentiful a region's resources, they will bring little income to its inhabitants while producers remain cut off from buyers.\n\nThe government must encourage production in both regions and open the routes along which their goods can travel. A common market allows different products to complement one another, and places with related industries to divide their work. If these businesses prosper, both regions will have reason to maintain their ties.
after.nesnd_small_regional_governance_journal_: Goods already pass between the regions, but the people who administer public affairs cannot all remain in one place. Taxes come from both regions, and administration and education need a footing in both. Otherwise, every increase in production will leave more local affairs to be decided far away.\n\nThe government needs people to undertake this work and schools to train their successors. Giving local inhabitants the skills to enter new occupations will spare the country from having to seek every capable official in the same few cities.
after.nesnd_small_order_journal_reason: Independence or extensive autonomy allows us to decide more of our own affairs. It also places a greater share of the burden of trade and defence on our government. People expect freedom from interference to bring some improvement in their lives.\n\nIndustries need materials and customers, the provinces need schools and administrators, and the army needs support. The wealth and abilities of our people must sustain these institutions if our political freedom is to endure.
after.nesnd_small_working_status: All conditions are met this month, adding to the total of qualifying months.
after.nesnd_small_paused_status: Some conditions are unmet this month. The total of qualifying months does not increase.
after.nesnd_small_dispute_journal_reason: Hardship is encouraging local people to seek a common remedy. Some demand changes to the ownership of land and the conditions of labour. Others want a greater voice in public affairs. Burdens once borne by each household alone are becoming the demands of a movement.\n\nThe government may allow them to organise, promise a response through legislation, or send the police to silence them. Those who enjoy the existing arrangements and those who seek to change them will judge from our response whose interests the government intends to defend.
after.nesnd_small_dispute_status: The local movement is still waiting for its demands to be addressed.
after.nesnd_small_public_desc: Local administration and industry need literate, skilled people. Fund a year of public provision to help residents qualify for new occupations.
after.nesnd_small_public_tt: Pay the weekly amount set at the start of the programme for 12 months, temporarily improving Qualifications Growth and Taxation Capacity. The programme cannot be cancelled early or started again while it is running.
after.nesnd_small_specialise_button_desc: Merchants and guilds hope to expand within the present market. Support their use of established trading routes to find more buyers for local production.
after.nesnd_small_specialise_button_tt: Qualifications Growth improves and Authority falls by 25 for 12 months. The arrangement ends if the market owner changes or we gain a market of our own.
after.nesnd_small_own_market_button: Prepare a Market of Our Own
after.nesnd_small_own_market_button_desc: Prepare a market of our own, taking responsibility for the supply of materials, production and the sale of our goods.
after.nesnd_small_own_market_button_tt: Preparations last 12 months and do not immediately change market ownership. If we already have our own market, public investment can begin. Qualifying industries must have no input shortages during preparations.
after.nesnd_small_retarget_button_desc: Set separate development targets for the most populous state and for the remaining populated states together.
after.nesnd_small_retarget_button_tt: Make the most populous state we own one region, and our remaining states the other, selecting new centres for both. Current regional qualifying months reset to zero. Another revision is unavailable for 24 months. Rewards already received cannot be claimed again.
after.nesnd_small_restore_geography_button_des: Bring the two homeland regions back into a common undertaking, restoring the recovered territories to the economic and public life of the country.
after.nesnd_small_restore_geography_button_tt: Once the original homeland regions again meet the population and regional-centre requirements, restore their development targets and begin accumulating qualifying months anew. The 24-month interval between revisions still applies.
after.nesnd_small_order_button_desc: Use our present autonomy to develop our laws, market, public services and defence.
after.nesnd_small_order_button_tt: Begin development as an independent or highly autonomous country, accumulating 24 qualifying months within 120 months. Qualifying months must be accumulated anew if our independent or subject status changes, or if we lose our high autonomy. The completion reward can be claimed only once.
after.nesnd_small_request_autonomy_desc: Point to the strength of our local economy and administration, and ask the overlord to let us manage more of our own affairs.
after.nesnd_small_request_autonomy_tt: Ask our direct overlord for greater autonomy. Approval increases autonomy, reduces Liberty Desire and establishes a truce with the overlord.
after.nesnd_small_request_independence_desc: Propose peaceful independence to the overlord, seeking a negotiated end to subjection and responsibility for our own domestic and foreign affairs.
after.nesnd_small_request_independence_tt: Ask our direct overlord to agree to peaceful independence. Diplomatic means of seeking autonomy remain available if the proposal is refused.
after.nesnd_small_request_market_desc: Ask the present market owner to let us establish our own market, taking responsibility for supply, demand and transport.
after.nesnd_small_request_market_tt: Ask the current [concept_market_owner] to allow a [concept_market] of our own. If no separate market has been established within thirty days of their agreement, the request will be treated as unsuccessful.

after.nesnd_small_defence_fra_tt: Propose a five-year defensive treaty. The treaty is concluded if the other country agrees.

after.nesnd_small_defence_neighbour_desc: Seek a friendly neighbour with whom to arrange common defence against attack.
after.nesnd_small_defence_neighbour_tt: Review the eligible neighbour with the best relations before deciding whether to propose a defensive treaty. If relations are equal, the country with the higher GDP is chosen.

after.nesnd_small_states.continue: There is still much to be done.
after.nesnd_small_states.2.d: Our existing industries are beginning to provide farmers and labourers with a steadier livelihood. Goods can reach the market, employers can pay wages, and more households can support themselves through their work.\n\nTheir greater security also gives the government a dependable source of taxation. Every sum entering the treasury was once part of a household's living. Peace in the provinces and stability at home require the people who create this wealth to be able to carry on their work.
after.nesnd_small_states.3.d: Administration and education now have foundations the country can sustain. Public affairs have people to attend to them, knowledge has a means of spreading, and local industries can hope to find workers trained for new occupations.\n\nThe more people learn, the more readily they can take part in national life and explain what they expect of their government. These institutions give the state more capable hands, while requiring those in power to attend more closely to the livelihoods of the governed.
after.nesnd_small_states.4.d: Our market relations have changed, bringing an end to the temporary arrangements under which merchants and enterprises operated in the former market. The supplies, customers and transport connections on which they relied must be secured under new circumstances.\n\nA government may change its direction, but producers must still find buyers for their goods. Their ability to carry on trading will shape employment and income in the provinces.
after.nesnd_small_states.5.d: Years have passed without the government bringing law, trade and local enterprise together to sustain its intended programme of self-government. Existing industries and schools can continue their work, but the conditions needed to support the country's affairs remain incomplete.\n\nThe undertaking must be deferred. It may be resumed when the necessary conditions are in place. Meanwhile, the wealth and skills already acquired will need to be sustained through the daily life of the country.
after.nesnd_small_states.6.d: Local industries can now support education and administration, and the country has the market connections and defensive strength needed to sustain its autonomy. With trained people and revenue at its disposal, the government has more to rely on in its dealings with foreign powers.\n\nThe public has paid for these achievements through taxes and labour. What people hope to receive in return is a country in which they can earn their living in peace.
after.nesnd_small_states.11.d: The government has enacted the legal reform it promised to the provinces. Those who organised to demand it now have reason to believe that they can influence national affairs. Practices they once had to endure can at last be challenged in the name of the law.\n\nThe beneficiaries of the old arrangements will hardly forget their loss. Political disputes will follow the new law into everyday life, and the government must ensure that its legislation is enforced.
after.nesnd_small_states.12.d: The promised deadline has passed, but the legal reform people awaited has still not arrived. The gentlemen in the capital asked the provinces for patience. The old restrictions remain, and they have little to show for the trust they demanded.\n\nThose who believed the government are losing faith. The passage of a deadline has done nothing to ease their hardships, and unanswered demands are hardening into deeper resentment...
after.nesnd_small_states.10.land: Hardship among local farmers and labourers is drawing support to the land reform movement. Ownership of the soil and control over labour determine how much they can keep after a year's work, and whether they can escape their old dependencies.\n\nThose who demand change have organised. To answer their demands, the government must challenge established rights and those who hold them. If we merely ask them to endure, what reason have they to place their trust in the present order?
after.nesnd_small_states.10.labor: Growing hardship among labourers has brought local support to the labour movement. Workers want a voice in wages, hours and protection at work, hoping to avoid facing their employers alone. Employers see demands that will alter their costs and their authority over labour.\n\nThe government must decide how to treat these organisations. Allowing workers to speak, promising legislation or sending in the police will shape the means by which both sides can defend their interests.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.representation: Local liberal and radical movements are seeking wider support. People excluded by their status or political qualifications want a voice in the affairs that govern their lives. Those who already hold power may have little desire to admit them.\n\nThe advocates of wider participation have organised, and the government can no longer leave the argument on paper. Whether it permits their activities and is prepared to change the law will determine how these people regard the state.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.organise: Let them organise and state their demands openly.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.organise_tt: The relevant movement gains #p +15%#! support weight and Authority falls by #n 25#! for #v 12 months#!. #v 1%#! of the affected population becomes Radical. A local character supporting the movement, if available, gains #p +10#! Popularity for #v 12 months#!.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.promise_land: We shall change the tenure of the land.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.promise_land_tt: Reform land tenure within 24 months by enacting Peasant Proprietorship, Commercialized Agriculture or Collectivized Agriculture. The relevant Interest Group gains +2 Approval while the promise remains in force. Enacting the reform in time gains Loyalists. If the deadline passes without reform and the demand remains unresolved, Radicals increase.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.promise_debt_tt: Abolish slavery through legislation within 24 months. The relevant Interest Group gains +2 Approval while the promise remains in force. Enacting the reform in time gains Loyalists. If the deadline passes without reform and the demand remains unresolved, Radicals increase.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.promise_labor: Working people deserve the protection of the law.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.promise_labor_tt: Reform labour rights within 24 months by enacting Regulatory Bodies or Workers' Protections. The relevant Interest Group gains +2 Approval while the promise remains in force. Enacting the reform in time gains Loyalists. If the deadline passes without reform and the demand remains unresolved, Radicals increase.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.promise_caste: We shall remove the restrictions of caste.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.promise_caste_tt: Reform the caste system within 24 months by enacting Caste Not Enforced or Affirmative Action. The relevant Interest Group gains +2 Approval while the promise remains in force. Enacting the reform in time gains Loyalists. If the deadline passes without reform and the demand remains unresolved, Radicals increase.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.promise_representa: Promise a wider voice in the affairs of the country.

Widen political participation within 24 months by enacting Wealth Voting, Census Suffrage or Universal Suffrage. The relevant Interest Group gains +2 Approval while the promise remains in force. Enacting the reform in time gains Loyalists. If the deadline passes without reform and the demand remains unresolved, Radicals increase.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.suppress: Send the police to put a stop to these organisations.
after.nesnd_small_states.10.suppress_tt: The relevant movement loses #n 15%#! support weight and Authority falls by #n 50#! for #v 12 months#!. #v 2%#! of the affected population becomes Radical.
after.nesnd_small_states.20.t: A Proposal from the Local Government
after.nesnd_small_states.20.autonomy: The government of [SCOPE.sCountry('canon_sender').GetName] points to progress in its economy and administration as grounds for managing more of its own affairs. It argues that it can now bear these responsibilities, and that the overlord's restrictions should be relaxed accordingly.\n\nAcceptance will grant the local government greater autonomy. We must judge whether less interference will preserve this relationship, and how much we are prepared to spend to retain our present authority.
after.nesnd_small_states.20.independence: [SCOPE.sCountry('canon_sender').GetName] seeks a negotiated end to subjection, with its own government assuming responsibility for domestic and foreign affairs. It hopes that recognition of independence will allow the two countries to live at peace.\n\nAgreement means relinquishing our overlordship and the disputes its maintenance might provoke. Their demand reaches beyond freedom to administer a few matters locally: they wish to decide the future of their country.
after.nesnd_small_states.20.market: [SCOPE.sCountry('canon_sender').GetName] has asked to establish a separate market and manage its own production and trade. Its merchants and producers would have to arrange their supplies and find their buyers, changing the existing exchange of goods between our countries.\n\nWe must decide whether to grant this freedom.
after.nesnd_small_states.20.defence: [SCOPE.sCountry('canon_sender').GetName] seeks a defensive treaty with our country. It hopes to gain an ally on whom it can depend, while we would gain a partner in resisting attacks from abroad.\n\nOnce a treaty is signed, an attack on our partner may bring us into war. This friendly proposal asks something of our army and treasury as well.
after.nesnd_small_refuse_tt: Refuse the proposal. Rejecting a request for greater autonomy increases the subject's Liberty Desire and harms relations.
after.nesnd_small_states.21.d: The government is preparing to propose a common defence agreement to [SCOPE.sCountry('small_receiver').GetName]. Relations are friendly and our territories lie close together. Armies able to support one another would give a foreign aggressor reason to hesitate.\n\nThe envoys have drawn up their proposal and await our decision.
after.nesnd_final_small_own_public_tt: We already own our market. If the public investment requirements are met, start the following 12-month investment.
after.nesnd_final_small_public_existing_tt: Public services: Taxation Capacity +10%, Qualifications Growth +15%. Total duration 12 months.

before.nesnd_hus_registration.1.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_khanate').GetName] has been established. Indigenous communities from Dongzhou and the United States are settling there, looking to their new khan to defend their lands. Washington and the government of Dongzhou reject the loss of this territory. War on the Plains is imminent.
before.nesnd_hus_registration.1.a: A new government stands on the Plains.
before.nesnd_hus_registration.2.d: After Indigenous registration was completed, Manchu and Mongol residents remained in the second tier. They have now left the republic: some for $CNE$, others for the American West, seeking a life on new ground.
before.nesnd_american_restoration_reason: The heirs of Moctezuma and the Andean court claim different inheritances. Both confront a question the republics have left unresolved: can Indigenous communities control their land and local government? Dynastic supporters appeal to old compacts, while rural communities resist dispossession. Recognition, negotiation, and repression offer sharply different futures.
before.nesnd_native_recognize: Recognize the Dynasty and Local Compacts
before.nesnd_native_recognize_desc: Bring the old dynasty and local communities into a new political settlement.
before.nesnd_native_recognize_tt: Restore an Indigenous monarchy. If an Inca court already exists, propose a union requiring its consent within ninety days.
before.nesnd_native_negotiate_desc: Seek rural cooperation through local councils and negotiations over land.
before.nesnd_native_negotiate_tt: Restoration Pressure falls by #p 15#! and any preparations for an uprising are halted. Local councils continue to ease support for restoration in the countryside.
before.nesnd_native_suppress_desc: Use the army to break up restorationist meetings and networks, temporarily weakening rural resistance.
before.nesnd_native_suppress_tt: Restoration Pressure falls by #p 20#!. #n 5%#! of our Indigenous population become [Concept('concept_radical','Radicals')].
before.nesnd_restoration_existing_court_status: The Inca court has been established. When both countries are independent and at peace, we may propose a union, subject to the other government's agreement.
before.nesnd_restoration_waiting_land_status: Restorationists seek a viable core. Territory, population, or current conflicts prevent a territorial uprising.
before.nesnd_restoration_politics_status: Dynastic supporters and local communities are gathering political support.
before.nesnd_native_restoration_war_reason: The restorationists have formed a government and demand that the central government surrender its authority. Both claim the same village lands and the allegiance of the same garrisons. Neither will make peace while its rival governs part of the country.
before.nesnd_restoration_war_status: Control of the provinces has yet to be confirmed.
before.nesnd_restoration_war_against: Our forces face [ROOT.GetCountry.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_restoration_opponent').GetCountry.GetName]. Victory requires the annexation of its territory.
before.nesnd_restoration_war_mustering: [ROOT.GetCountry.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_restoration_opponent').GetCountry.GetName] still holds territory. Both sides are mustering their forces.
before.dp_nesnd_native_restoration_desc: The Indigenous polity and the former government contest rule over the country. The victor will annex its opponent.
before.wg_nesnd_restoration_settlement_desc: Defeat the opposing government and annex its entire territory. The defeat of an Indigenous polity may drive some residents to flee and political figures into exile.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.1.d: Supporters of the old dynasty and local armed groups have established a separate government. Both sides demand the other’s territory, and the restoration dispute has become a war. The communities seek to defend their land and local authority, while the restorationists seek the dynasty’s return.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.2.d: Indigenous communities displaced by repression have crossed the border, bringing family ties, local organizations, and memories of lost homes. Their destinations will anchor new refuge networks, though arrival does not immediately restore their livelihoods.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.3.d: The army has broken up restorationist meetings and disrupted contact among local leaders. Military officers support the government’s use of force, while resentment has deepened in the countryside. Supporters of the old dynasty remain, and the communities’ demands for land and local authority are unanswered.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.4.d: The old dynasty has returned to the center of political life. Local communities have offered their support in pursuit of recognition for their land and representatives. Relations among court, assembly, and countryside will now develop under the new settlement.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.5.d: The rival government has lost its last territory, and the country is reunited. The newly acquired provinces still bear the wounds of war. Disputed land and the fate of those driven into exile now require the government's attention.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.5.a: Take responsibility for the country left by war.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.6.d: This struggle has not brought unification. The government must reconsider its relations with local powers in light of the present borders.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.10.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_restoration_applicant').GetName] proposes recognizing the existing Inca court and joining our state. Union would end the partition and bring its local communities into the political settlement we must uphold.
before.nesnd_khanate_emergence_reason: The American Civil War has shaken authority on the Great Plains. Dongzhou's new registration law has stirred Indigenous resentment, and community leaders are rallying supporters of the earlier uprising to establish a khanate of their own.
before.nesnd_khanate_waiting_status: Awaiting four connected, populated American states on the Great Plains. The United States must retain populated territory after cession.
before.nesnd_khanate_established_tt: The Indigenous khanate has actually received four states and established its government.
before.nesnd_khanate_survival_reason: Both the United States and Dongzhou demand the khanate's territory. The new khan must lead its communities against both powers and defend the lands on which their people have settled.
before.nesnd_khanate_usa_status: The United States has not ended its intervention against the khanate.
before.nesnd_khanate_hus_status: Dongzhou has not ended its intervention against the khanate.
before.nesnd_khanate_survival_status: Both interventions against the khanate have ended.
before.nesnd_khanate_survived_tt: The khanate survives and both independent interventions have reached an outcome.
before.nesnd_suppress_native_khanate_reason: Territorial cession and migration have changed the balance of power in North America. Our government seeks to annex the khanate, while the khanate intends to force its interveners to acknowledge its position.
before.nesnd_khanate_intervention_status: Our government is seeking to annex the khanate.
before.nesnd_khanate_destroyed_tt: Our country has annexed the Great Plains Khanate.
before.nesnd_khanate_suppression_failed_tt: The intervention has ended without annexation of the khanate by our country.
before.nesnd_khanate_war: War of Intervention on the Plains
before.dp_nesnd_khanate_suppression: War of Intervention on the Plains
before.dp_nesnd_khanate_suppression_desc: The intervening power demands annexation of the Great Plains Khanate; the khanate demands the humiliation of its opponent.
before.wg_nesnd_khanate_humiliation_desc: Force the government responsible for this intervention to accept humiliation.
before.nesnd_native_american_republic_desc: Unite the Americas and Greenland. Once the former state has ceased to exist, establish a republic with Indigenous primary cultures and a complete ordinary legal settlement.
before.nesnd_native_khanate.2.d: Both interventions have ended, and the khanate has preserved its government. Communities united to resist outside powers must now settle questions of taxation, defence and local authority if the plains compact is to endure.
before.nesnd_native_khanate.2.a: Preserve the state we have built.
before.nesnd_native_khanate.3.d: From the northern plains to the southern mountains, the Americas now answer to one government. The old state of Dongzhou is gone. The new [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] has taken its name, abolished its social hierarchy and proclaimed republican government across the continent.
before.nesnd_native_khanate.3.a: Let the peoples of America shape their future.
before.nesnd_a2_exodus_both_desc: Manchu and Mongol communities have left for [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_cne_country').GetName] or the west of [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_usa_country').GetName]. Each community has a seventy percent chance of choosing the former and thirty percent the latter. Community sizes differ, so the actual population is not divided in an exact seventy-to-thirty ratio.
before.nesnd_a2_exodus_cne_desc: No receiving destination remains in the American west. The Manchu and Mongol communities have all moved to [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_cne_country').GetName], and the planned division between two destinations has not taken place.
before.nesnd_a2_exodus_usa_desc: No receiving destination remains in the east. The Manchu and Mongol communities have all moved to western [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_usa_country').GetName], and the planned division between two destinations has not taken place.
before.nesnd_a2_exodus_none_desc: Neither destination can receive the Manchu and Mongol communities. They remain where they live, and this migration has ended. The registration choice already enacted remains in force.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.11.d: The Inca court did not consent to union within the allotted time. Both states retain their governments and territory. Negotiations may be renewed after the waiting period.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.12.d: The Inca court has declined the union offer. A shared dynastic tradition has not proved sufficient to end the partition. Talks may resume after the waiting period.
before.nesnd_restore_native_hus_desc: Unite the Americas and Greenland. Once the former state has ceased to exist, establish a republic with Indigenous primary cultures and a complete ordinary legal settlement.
before.nesnd_native_americas_unified_tt: Own every region in the Americas and Greenland in full, including uncolonized land and foreign portions of split states.
before.nesnd_native_hus_restored_tt: Adopt Indigenous primary cultures, establish a republic, and enact the complete settlement of twenty-four ordinary law groups.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.13.d: Dynastic supporters have reconvened the local communities to settle relations among court, local representatives, and countryside. The existing state will continue under a renewed political compact, bearing the divisions left by the earlier war.
before.nesnd_american_restoration.13.a: Preserve the state and renew its compact.
before.nesnd_native_khanate.2.both: Both intervening governments have been forced to accept humiliation, and the khanate retains its government. Victory has lent prestige to the Plains compact. Its communities must now turn their wartime alliance into lasting government.
before.nesnd_native_khanate.2.one: One intervention ended with the opponent's humiliation, and the other has also come to a close. The khanate has preserved its government. The plains communities must now carry their wartime cooperation into everyday rule.
before.nesnd_native_khanate.2.none: Both interventions have ended. Though it has forced neither opponent to accept humiliation, the khanate has preserved its government. Its communities must share the burdens of taxation and defence to sustain the new state.

Local leaders are gathering people and supplies, seeking a new government that will protect their lands and autonomy.\n\nThese preparations will take twelve months. Local support and the prospect of an agreement on councils and land rights will determine whether the communities take up arms.

after.nesnd_hus_registration.1.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_khanate').GetName] has been established. Indigenous settlers from Dongzhou and the United States have brought their families, possessions and hopes of keeping their land to the new country. The khan chosen by their communities depends on their support, and must defend the homes they have found.\n\nThe United States refuses to relinquish the territory it has lost, while Dongzhou also lays claim to these plains. For the settlers, the khanate's survival will decide whether they can remain here or must uproot their lives once more.
after.nesnd_hus_registration.2.d: After Indigenous registration was completed, Manchu and Mongol residents remained in the second tier. They have now left the republic: some for $CNE$, others for the American West, seeking a life on new ground.
after.nesnd_american_restoration_reason: The restoration of the house of Moctezuma and the Andean court has won support among Indigenous villages. The republics promised liberty, yet their new rulers still encroach on common land and exact taxes. For those who work the fields, a change of flag in the capital has done little to lighten their burden.\n\nSupporters of the old dynasties are turning this resentment to their advantage. They promise to protect common land and local rights in return for the villages' people and arms. Rural communities, in turn, hope to use a monarch's prestige to resist the depredations of the new elite. The government must decide whether to recognise the dynasty, draw away its supporters through local councils and land reform, or send the army to silence the calls for restoration.
after.nesnd_native_recognize: Recognize the Dynasty and Local Compacts
after.nesnd_native_recognize_desc: Recognise the rule of the old dynasty, allowing the court and local communities to negotiate a renewed political compact.
after.nesnd_native_recognize_tt: Restore an Indigenous monarchy. If an Inca court already exists, propose a union requiring its consent within ninety days.
after.nesnd_native_negotiate_desc: Discuss land rights and local councils with community representatives, so that rural demands can find an answer under the present government.
after.nesnd_native_negotiate_tt: Restoration Pressure falls by #p 15#! and any preparations for an uprising are halted. Local councils continue to ease support for restoration in the countryside.
after.nesnd_native_suppress_desc: Use the army to break up restorationist meetings and networks, temporarily weakening rural resistance.
after.nesnd_native_suppress_tt: Restoration Pressure falls by #p 20#!. #n 5%#! of our Indigenous population become [Concept('concept_radical','Radicals')].
after.nesnd_restoration_existing_court_status: The Inca court has been established. When both countries are independent and at peace, we may propose a union, subject to the other government's agreement.
after.nesnd_restoration_waiting_land_status: The restorationists are seeking a core territory from which to rise. Land, population or the present wars still prevent them from breaking away to form a state.
after.nesnd_restoration_politics_status: Supporters of the old dynasty are seeking rural backing through demands for land and local rights.
after.nesnd_native_restoration_war_reason: The restorationists have formed a separate government, bringing village militias together under the old dynasty's name to claim rule over the whole country. The former government refuses to surrender the territory that has broken away. War will now decide who protects the common lands, who collects the taxes and whose orders the army obeys.\n\nBoth sides intend to annex their opponent and refuse a peace that leaves the country divided. The victorious government will also have to answer the political demands of those who fought in its cause.
after.nesnd_restoration_war_status: Sovereignty over the country and its lands remains in dispute.
after.nesnd_restoration_war_against: Our forces are contesting rule over the country with [ROOT.GetCountry.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_restoration_opponent').GetCountry.GetName]. We seek to annex our opponent and end the division into two states.
after.nesnd_restoration_war_mustering: [ROOT.GetCountry.MakeScope.Var('nesnd_restoration_opponent').GetCountry.GetName] still governs its territory. Both sides are mustering forces to pursue their claims to rule.
after.dp_nesnd_native_restoration_desc: The Indigenous polity and the former government contest rule over the country. The victor will annex its opponent.
after.wg_nesnd_restoration_settlement_desc: Defeat the opposing government and annex its entire territory. The defeat of an Indigenous polity may drive some residents to flee and political figures into exile.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.1.d: The restorationists have established their own government. The old dynasty's name has drawn local militias to its cause, while village leaders hope the uprising will secure their common lands and autonomy. Those who once demanded concessions now demand that the government surrender the country.\n\nThe capital is equally unwilling to accept partition. Both sides seek to annex the other and refuse a peace that leaves two governments in place. Their struggle for authority has become a fight to the finish.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.2.d: Indigenous communities fleeing repression have crossed the border, bringing their families, local organisations and memories of a lost homeland. The places that receive them will become centres of a new network of refuge. Open land offers them somewhere to settle and, at last, to rest, if they can survive long enough to learn the ways of this unfamiliar country.\n\nIn time, perhaps their lives here may be better than those they left behind.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.2.a: May the Earth Mother bless us, and keep the soil fertile beneath the sun...
after.nesnd_american_restoration.3.d: The army has dispersed restorationist gatherings and disrupted contacts among local leaders. Advocates of force applaud the government for asserting its authority at last. The Indigenous people facing searches and arrests have further cause to believe that this government protects only those who seize their land.\n\nThe restoration movement has lost ground for the moment, but resentment in the countryside has deepened. Supporters of the old dynasty who escaped the soldiers are unlikely to let such an opportunity pass.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.3.a: The army has acted. The countryside may yet refuse to submit.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.4.d: The old dynasty has regained rule over the country. Village communities support the court, which upholds their local rights to preserve the compact. Representatives once turned away by the capital now have somewhere to bring their demands.\n\nThe monarch's power will depend on these people. Whether raising taxes or recruiting soldiers, the restored dynasty must remember whose support brought it back.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.4.a: The dynasty rests on the villages that support it.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.5.d: The opposing government has lost its last territory, and the country is reunited. The army is taking control of the provinces. Taxes collected by rival authorities during the war will once again be sent to a single capital.\n\nMany in the countryside supported the defeated side. The lowering of its flag will hardly change their convictions. The government must decide how to treat these people and the demands for which they took up arms.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.5.a: Restore order in the provinces first.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.6.d: Changes in territory and government have interrupted the restoration struggle. Our former rival can no longer continue the fight, yet we have not taken possession of all its lands.\n\nThe government must reassess its friends and enemies in these altered circumstances. Unresolved local questions will have to be addressed within the new borders.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.6.a: First establish who now rules these lands.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.10.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_restoration_applicant').GetName] proposes that both countries recognise the existing Inca court and that its territory be joined to ours. A shared dynastic tradition has given their representatives and ours a basis on which to discuss union.\n\nTheir local communities will enter our rule along with the land. They look to the court to uphold common land and local rights, and await our answer.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.10.a: Let one court preside over one country.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.10.b: A shared tradition is not yet enough to unite our states.
after.nesnd_khanate_emergence_reason: The American Civil War has shaken authority on the Great Plains, while Dongzhou's new registration law has brought Indigenous grievances to the fore. Community leaders are renewing ties with supporters of the earlier uprising, hoping to use the upheaval in both countries to establish a khanate of their own.\n\nLand holds this alliance together. Migration and registration determine where people may live and who decides their status. To win the communities' support, a new khan must promise to defend these rights and possess the strength to resist intervention by both powers.
after.nesnd_khanate_waiting_status: Awaiting four connected, populated American states on the Great Plains. The United States must retain populated territory after cession.
after.nesnd_khanate_established_tt: The Indigenous khanate has received four states and established its government.
after.nesnd_khanate_survival_reason: The United States and Dongzhou both demand the khanate's annexation. Indigenous people who have only just settled on the Plains must take up arms again to defend the homes they struggled to obtain. Having acclaimed a common khan, the communities expect him to unite their scattered forces against the two invaders.\n\nThe new khan needs their recruits and supplies, while local leaders insist on retaining their rights. War has brought these peoples together. Whether their union can hold will determine whether they can remain on these plains.
after.nesnd_khanate_usa_status: The United States has not ended its intervention against the khanate.
after.nesnd_khanate_hus_status: Dongzhou has not ended its intervention against the khanate.
after.nesnd_khanate_survival_status: Both interventions against the khanate have ended.
after.nesnd_khanate_survived_tt: The khanate survives, and both separate interventions have ended.
after.nesnd_suppress_native_khanate_reason: Territorial cession and migration on the Great Plains have changed the balance of power in North America. With the support of Indigenous communities, the khanate has established a government and seeks to bind settlers, land and local militias into a new state. The longer we allow it to take root, the harder our territorial claims will be to uphold.\n\nOur government intends to end the khanate's rule through annexation. The new khan hopes to force the intervening powers to submit and win prestige for the Plains Compact. At stake are both the territory itself and the right to determine the lives of its Indigenous inhabitants.
after.nesnd_khanate_intervention_status: Our government is seeking to annex the khanate.
after.nesnd_khanate_destroyed_tt: Our country has annexed the Great Plains Khanate.
after.nesnd_khanate_suppression_failed_tt: The dispute over the Great Plains has ended. Our country has not annexed the khanate.
after.nesnd_khanate_war: War of Intervention on the Plains
after.dp_nesnd_khanate_suppression: War of Intervention on the Plains
after.dp_nesnd_khanate_suppression_desc: The intervening power demands the annexation of the Great Plains Khanate. The khanate demands the humiliation of its opponent.
after.wg_nesnd_khanate_humiliation_desc: Force the government responsible for this intervention to accept humiliation.
after.nesnd_native_american_republic_desc: Unite the Americas and Greenland. Once the former state has ceased to exist, establish a republic with Indigenous primary cultures and enact its republican laws.
after.nesnd_native_khanate.2.d: Both interventions have ended, and the khanate has preserved its government. The communities joined forces to resist outside powers, and those who migrated here can now remain and build their lives on the Plains.\n\nThe new khan must reach agreement with local leaders on taxation, defence and authority. Disagreements set aside while they fought together will return in the course of everyday government. The Plains Compact will endure only so long as the state serves the interests of those who sustain it.
after.nesnd_native_khanate.2.a: We defended these plains together. We must govern them together.
after.nesnd_native_khanate.3.d: From the northern plains to the southern mountains, the Americas now answer to one government. The former state of Dongzhou is gone. The new [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] has inherited its name, abolished the old social hierarchy and assumed rule over the continent as a republic.\n\nIndigenous peoples who once petitioned for land, status and local rights have become the masters of this country. This vast republic is now their responsibility. They must decide how common laws will enter the lives of its many communities, and whose interests their newly acquired power will protect.
after.nesnd_native_khanate.3.a: Let the peoples of America shape their future.
after.nesnd_a2_exodus_both_desc: With registration complete, Manchu and Mongol communities left in the second tier have begun to leave the republic. Some have gone to [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_cne_country').GetName], others to the west of [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_usa_country').GetName], carrying their families and old ties to new lands.\n\nEach community has a seventy percent chance of choosing the former destination and thirty percent of choosing the latter. Along with their people and possessions, the republic is losing the hopes they once held of an equal place within it.
after.nesnd_a2_exodus_cne_desc: The American West has nowhere left to receive these migrants. All the Manchu and Mongol communities leaving the republic have gone to [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_cne_country').GetName]. Registration failed to give them the standing they had hoped for, and migration became a means of seeking a different life.\n\nFamilies and old connections travel east with them. Others will tend the homes they leave behind.
after.nesnd_a2_exodus_usa_desc: No destination in the east can receive these migrants. All the Manchu and Mongol communities leaving the republic have gone to the west of [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_usa_country').GetName]. They carry their families and possessions to new lands, hoping to leave their second-tier status behind.\n\nWhat opportunities await them will become clear only after they arrive. Their former homes are already behind them.
after.nesnd_a2_exodus_none_desc: The Manchu and Mongol communities have found no place to receive them in the east and cannot move to the American West. They must remain in their present homes, living under the status assigned to them by registration.\n\nTheir plans to leave have come to nothing. The grievances that prompted them have not.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.11.d: The allotted time has passed without the Inca court agreeing to union. A shared dynastic tradition has not brought the two governments under a single authority. Each remains responsible for its own people and territory.\n\nLocal communities must reconcile their hopes for the court with the politics of the present. Talks may be renewed, but an unanswered proposal cannot alter the fact that two states still stand.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.12.d: The Inca court has refused the proposal for union. A common dynastic tradition may draw the two sides closer, but it has not persuaded their present rulers to accept a single state.\n\nOur government must continue to address land and local politics at home, rather than entrust these responsibilities to a reply from the court. Talks may be renewed once the waiting period has ended.
after.nesnd_restore_native_hus_desc: Unite the Americas and Greenland. Once the former state has ceased to exist, establish a republic with Indigenous primary cultures and enact its republican laws.
after.nesnd_native_americas_unified_tt: Own every region in the Americas and Greenland in full, including uncolonized land and foreign portions of split states.
after.nesnd_native_hus_restored_tt: Establish a republic with Indigenous primary cultures and enact laws in all twenty-four ordinary law groups.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.13.d: The dynasty's supporters have summoned local communities anew to discuss the political arrangements between court and countryside. The cause of restoration is established, but local leaders still want to know what place their lands and representatives will have under its rule.\n\nThe country must live with the divisions left by earlier struggles. The court needs rural support, and the countryside demands protection for its interests. Their compact will have reason to endure only when these claims take effect in everyday government.
after.nesnd_american_restoration.13.a: Preserve the state and renew its compact.
after.nesnd_native_khanate.2.both: Both intervening governments have been forced to accept humiliation, and the khanate has preserved its government. The victory of the Army of the Plains Compact has brought prestige to the union between the new khan and the communities. Settlers can remain in their new homes.\n\nWar united them against outside powers. They must now agree on taxation, the burdens of defence and the rights retained by each community. The Plains Compact will need more than past victories to become a lasting government.
after.nesnd_native_khanate.2.one: One intervention ended in the opponent's humiliation, and the other has also come to a close. The khanate has preserved its government and territory. Those who settled here can remain and earn their living on the Plains.\n\nThe communities gathered beneath the new khan's banner to resist invasion. They must now discuss taxation, defence and local authority. In peacetime, those who shared the burdens of war will need to see what the common undertaking offers them in return.
after.nesnd_native_khanate.2.none: Both interventions have ended. The khanate forced neither opponent to accept humiliation, but it has preserved its government. The communities of the Plains can continue to build their new homes.\n\nThe new khan still depends on local leaders and settlers for support. How taxes and defence are shared, and how local rights are protected, will determine how long this compact for survival can endure.

after.nesnd_native_khanate.4.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_khanate_opponent').GetName] has withdrawn from treaties with the khanate containing an alliance or defensive pact, clearing the way for intervention. Promises once intended to secure both countries have given way to demands for annexation and territory.\n\nAny trade or other provisions within those treaties end with them, and the withdrawing country bears the cost of breaking its word. A relationship on which the khanate could once rely has broken under the preparations for war.
after.nesnd_native_khanate.4.a: The war begins with a broken promise.
